source_title: \vspace{-1.5cm}Perfect Matching in Product Graphs\\ and in their Random Subgraphs
title: In the random subgraph of a high-dimensional product graph there is typically no component whose order lies in the interval from two to d to the twentieth

standard_prerequisites.name: The parameters n, d, p and the constant M, the relation d = Theta_M(log n), and the low-degree expansion estimates of the product graph
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's preliminaries and proof outline (source lines 201-240); the hypothesis n(1-p)^d <= d^{1/50} used at the end of the proof is the author's displayed eq:mu-range cited below as a pointer
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the expansion bound e_G(K,K^c) >= k(d - (M-1) log_M k) applied to a set K of size k, and the parameter relations that turn the probability bound into n^{1-0.8k}.

core_obligations: Expansion of a set of size k: for every K of size k between 2 and d^20 the author's expansion estimate gives e_G(K,K^c) >= k(d - (M-1) log_M k) >= 0.9kd (proof lines 519-523).

Modelling a component of order k: if K is a component of G_p then it contains a spanning tree whose k-1 edges are present while all e_G(K,K^c) cut edges are absent, which is the event whose probability the rooted-tree bound controls (proof lines 524-525).

The probability bound: using the rooted-tree bound the author bounds the probability that G_p has a component of order k by n(ed)^{k-1}(1-p)^{0.9kd}, then uses 2 <= k <= d^20, n(1-p)^d <= d^{1/50} and d = Theta_M(log n) to get n^{1-0.8k} (proof lines 525-530).
Union bound over k: summing the exponential bound over all k in the interval shows that with high probability no such component exists (proof lines 531-532).
proof_roadmap: 先对大小为 k 的集合用展开估计把割压到 0.9kd 以上。
再对 k-1 条边出现、全部割边不出现这一事件用有根树计数，得到 n(ed)^{k-1}(1-p)^{0.9kd}，代入参数关系化为 n^{1-0.8k}，最后对 k 求和。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the gap lemma for component orders (author lemma at source lines 514-516, label lem:component-gap): with high probability the random subgraph has no component whose order lies between 2 and d^20. The proof (source lines 518-532) is a first-moment computation whose content is the combination of two estimates: the expansion bound e_G(K,K^c) >= 0.9kd for sets of that size, coming from the author's displayed expansion estimate, and the rooted-tree bound that turns the event of K being a component into the product n(ed)^{k-1}(1-p)^{0.9kd}, after which the author substitutes 2 <= k <= d^20, n(1-p)^d <= d^{1/50} and d = Theta_M(log n) to reach n^{1-0.8k} and concludes with a union bound over k (proof lines 525-532). The estimates are quantitative and are the substance of the argument. H2.
